structural.note: Duration checks identify source-label inconsistencies, not semantic errors; original boundary rounding/annotation policy may contribute.

47.observation: Published frames show laptop upright around 10.55s, lowered/closed around 11.59s, then placed on sofa around 13.72s, all within/near the original 6.7-16.4s label.
47.conclusion: Text difference alone is not enough to call an annotation error; both captions describe a connected sequence.

1782.observation: The picture is taken from the table around 15.54-16.58s, held afterwards, and moved back toward the table around 29.04-30.08s. GT 25.7-32.0s is the return phase, but FIG asks about lifting.
1782.conclusion: Strong evidence of a manipulation-phase reversal in the fine query paired with inherited return-phase GT. No replacement interval is assigned.

1628.observation: Inside GT 13.8-23.5s, a cup is at the mouth around 14.17s and food is brought to the mouth around 18.33-20.33s.
1628.conclusion: Eating and drinking coexist. The action-word difference does not establish that the fine query is false in the labeled clip.

1697.observation: Door opening appears near 0.98-1.96s; the late GT 16.8-30.4s mostly shows laptop interaction. All three original coarse rows for this video refer to door opening under that same late interval.
1697.conclusion: Fine caption fits the published late frames better than coarse caption. Could reflect original coarse/time annotation or source alignment problems; raw video has not been independently verified. Do not force FIG back to coarse wording.

2293.observation: At the end of the clip, the person rises from the toilet around 43.83s and moves toward/out of the doorway around 44.83-47.0s. GT 43.3-48.0s is labeled walking out in original STA; fine query says entering and preparing to clean.
2293.conclusion: Strong evidence of exit/entry reversal and unsupported preparation-to-clean detail in the fine query; preserve official labels for evaluation.

81.observation: Original STA has sitting at table at 6.4-11.1s and pouring at 8.9-23.2s. Existing processor-RGB review shows pouring posture at 15.43s, beyond the sitting label. Some pouring also overlaps the sitting label.
81.conclusion: The sitting-row FIG query foregrounds pouring but inherits the sitting interval. Strong scope-mismatch risk, not proof that every frame inside GT lacks pouring.
